rejected_recommendation.evidence_assessment: The provided evidence is guideline-level (MISEV2023) that defines expectations but does not supply any SGL-001–specific CMC, assay validation, manufacturing, stability/potency correlation, or bridging biodistribution data. Confidence in program readiness is low until the requested program data are submitted and reviewed.
findings: MISEV2023 (ev-misev2023-quality-framework) provides consensus requirements for orthogonal EV characterization, separation from non-vesicular particles, documented production controls, and validated assays to support identity/potency claims.

No program-specific CMC or analytical validation data for SGL-001 were provided: MCB/WCB records, assay validation (LLOQ/specificity/precision), stability-indicating potency with in vivo PD correlation, GMP-like batch CoAs, and controlled large-animal intact-EV biodistribution data are absent.
Given the missing program data, claims that SGL-001 is production-ready, analytically validated, or bridged across species/lots are unsupported.
objections: The supplied evidence is only an expert-consensus guidance (MISEV2023); it does not demonstrate any program-specific CMC, analytical validation, batch comparability, stability–potency correlation, or controlled large-animal intact-EV biodistribution data required to justify advancing SGL-001 across-lot or cross-species comparability or intranasal formulation advancement.

claim_updates.rationale: MISEV2023 establishes these requirements as consensus best practice; however, program-level evidence is still required to demonstrate compliance.
claim_updates.statement: Orthogonal characterization, separation from non‑vesicular particles, and documented production controls are required before advancing formulation comparability or claiming reproducible intact‑EV identity/potency across lots.

claim_updates.rationale: No program-specific manufacturing records, MCB/WCB documentation, or multi-batch comparability data were provided to support this claim; therefore the assertion that scalability/reproducibility are demonstrated is unsupported.
claim_updates.statement: SGL-001 source cell scalability and reproducible production (MCB/WCB and multi-batch comparability) have been demonstrated.

decision_update.question: Should SGL-001 proceed to cross‑lot/cross‑species intact‑EV comparability testing and intranasal formulation advancement now?
decision_update.rationale: Insufficient program-specific CMC and analytical validation evidence. A Stage‑1 CMC/analytics package must be assembled and reviewed prior to comparability/advancement. Major therapeutic advancement requires human approval.

proposed_changes.editorial_clarification: MISEV2023 is consensus guidance that sets expectations but is not program-specific evidence. Statements that SGL-001 meets MISEV-derived gates require submission of SGL-001–specific records and validations.

hypothesis_update.rationale: MISEV2023 supports this gate-level hypothesis; program-specific validations are needed to test/close the hypothesis.
hypothesis_update.statement: A validated identity/potency/CMC framework is required to justify cross‑lot and cross‑species intact‑EV comparability and formulation advancement for SGL‑001.

proposed_changes.next_action: Assemble a Stage‑1 CMC/analytics package before any cross-lot/cross-species comparability or formulation advancement that includes: 1) MCB/WCB creation and characterization records (identity, sterility, adventitious agent testing); 2) defined orthogonal QC panel and validated assay reports (particle concentration/size, protein/lipid markers, non-vesicular contaminants) with LLOQ, specificity, precision, accuracy, and fit‑for‑purpose statements; 3) validated intact‑EV assays (demonstrating measurement of intact vesicles vs free label/non-vesicular particles); 4) a stability‑indicating, mechanism‑linked potency assay with demonstrated correlation to an in vivo PD endpoint; 5) CoAs and manufacturing records for ≥3 GMP-like production runs with comparability analyses; 6) controlled bridging biodistribution/toxicology study reports in a relevant large‑animal model using orthogonal intact‑EV detection and appropriate negative/artefact controls. After submission, request regulatory scientific advice/pre-IND. Do not run cross-species comparability or formulation advancement until package is reviewed and approved by humans.

risk_updates.description: Absence of MCB/WCB documentation, validated orthogonal assays, stability‑indicating potency with in vivo correlation, and multi‑batch comparability increases risk of uncontrolled product variability and misinterpreted biological effects.
risk_updates.mitigation: Assemble Stage‑1 CMC/analytics package and validate assays/batches per next action; do not proceed to cross‑lot/species comparability until mitigations completed and reviewed.
risk_updates.title: Insufficient CMC/identity/potency characterization

risk_updates.description: Without orthogonal intact‑EV assays validated across species and controlled large‑animal biodistribution with artefact controls, intranasal biodistribution signals may reflect free label or non‑vesicular particles.
risk_updates.mitigation: Perform controlled bridging biodistribution in a relevant large animal using orthogonal intact‑EV detection methods and negative/artefact controls as specified in next action.
risk_updates.title: Cross‑species intact‑EV biodistribution artefact risk

risk_updates.description: Efficacy signals observed in preclinical models may not generalize if product identity/potency are not quantitatively controlled across lots/species.
risk_updates.mitigation: Establish validated potency assay with in vivo PD correlation and verify CQA consistency across batches before broader efficacy generalization or clinical translation.
risk_updates.title: Limited translatability of preclinical efficacy without validated potency and identity measures

rejected_recommendation.recommendation: Do not proceed with cross-lot or cross-species intact-EV comparability testing or with intranasal formulation advancement for SGL-001 at this time. Assemble a Stage‑1 CMC/analytics package (see next action). When the package is complete, request regulatory scientific advice/pre-IND and require human approval before any major therapeutic advancement decision. Therapeutic advancement decision: requires human approval and remains pending.
